physical_harm: Deceased died on the spot; PW6 and PW7 sustained bleeding injuries
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence of PW1, PW3, PW5, PW6, and PW7, including their testimonies as eye-witnesses and injured eye-witnesses, and noted that there were no major/material contradictions in their depositions.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their evidence cannot be discarded solely because they were relatives of the deceased, and that PW6, as an injured eye-witness, had greater reliability and credibility.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 18.01.2007; Trial judgment: 21.02.2018; High Court decision: 21.02.2018; Supreme Court decision: 07.03.2022
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: A. Sirajudeen, Sanjeev Kumar, Mahfooz Ahsan Nazki, Polanki Gowtham, Shaik Mohamad Haneef, T. Vijaya Bhaskar Reddy, K. V. Girish Chowdary, Ms. Rajeswari Mukherjee; Counsel for the State: Guntur Prabhakar, D. Ramakrishna Reddy, Mrs. D. Bharathi Reddy, M. A. Chinnasamy, C. Rubavathi, M. Veeraraga van, C. Raghavendren, Ch. Leela Sarveswar, V. Senthil Kumar, P. Rajaram, K. Ethiraj, Goli Ramakrishna, Sumanth Nookala
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted accused no. 1 to 3, acquitted accused no. 4 to 11; High Court: Reversed conviction of accused no. 1 to 3, confirmed acquittal of accused no. 4 to 11; Supreme Court: Allowed appeals against acquittal of accused no. 1 to 3, dismissed appeals against acquittal of accused no. 4 to 11
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the High Court erred in acquitting accused Nos. 1 to 3, as the evidence of the eye-witnesses and injured eye-witnesses was consistent and reliable, the FIR was lodged within 24 hours as required, and the High Court unnecessarily gave weightage to minor contradictions.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court correctly acquitted accused Nos. 1 to 3 due to the interpolation in the FIR, the credibility of the witnesses being questioned, and the possibility of false implication of the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the credibility of witnesses cannot be discarded solely because they are relatives of the deceased, and that minor contradictions in testimony do not necessarily undermine the prosecution's case.
precedent_relied_upon: The Supreme Court relied on its own previous decisions regarding the reliability of injured eye-witnesses and the admissibility of FIRs lodged within the required time frame.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the High Court's acquittal of accused Nos. 1 to 3 was deemed erroneous, and the trial court's conviction and sentencing were restored.
other_sentence_order: Accused Nos. 1 to 3 were directed to surrender to undergo the remaining sentence within four weeks.
